question: What does the Matrice 30T manual say about altitude and obstacles during Failsafe RTH?

intake.reason: Seeking guidance on altitude limits and obstacle handling during Failsafe Return-To-Home per Matrice 30T manual

brief.short_answer: FAA guidance: In hazard cases, attempts to reestablish control link and use emergency procedures for loss of control link. DJI Matrice 30T manual: RTH altitude must be higher than obstacles; states failsafe RTH cannot avoid obstacles in low light and allows manual control if remote signal is normal; notes monitoring liveview and altitude when GNSS bars are limited. Incident reports: no usable evidence for DJI Matrice 30T in approved collection. Main gap/conflict: FAA allows remote-PIC to change routing/altitude during automated flight, while the manual asserts obstacle avoidance failure in low light during failsafe RTH, and there is no evidence about persistence of RTH after remote control restoration.

claims.text: When a hazard occurs, "Try to reestablish control link connection with the small unmanned aircraft. If connection cannot be reestablished, start emergency or contingency procedures for loss of control link."
claims.quote: Try to reestablish control link connection with the small unmanned aircraft. If connection cannot be reestablished, start emergency or contingency procedures for loss of control link.

claims.text: AC 107-2A Appendix A requires describing what will be done if the hazard occurs, e.g., "Describe what will be done if the hazard occurs."
claims.quote: Describe what will be done if the hazard occurs.

claims.text: During automated flight, the remote PIC must have the ability to change routing/altitude or command the aircraft to land immediately.
claims.quote: During automated flight, the remote PIC must have the ability to change routing/altitude or command the aircraft to land immediately.

claims.text: The remote PIC may transmit a command for the automated aircraft to climb, descend, land now, proceed to a new waypoint, enter an orbit pattern, or return to home.
claims.quote: The remote PIC may transmit a command for the automated aircraft to climb, descend, land now, proceed to a new waypoint, enter an orbit pattern, or return to home.
conditions: to avoid a hazard or give right-of-way

claims.text: The remote PIC assuming control of the small UAS maintains responsibility for the safe operation of the small UAS.
claims.quote: The remote PIC assuming control of the small UAS maintains responsibility for the safe operation of the small UAS.

claims.text: The RTH altitude is related to the Home Point; Make sure the RTH altitude is higher than any obstacle in the area.
claims.quote: The RTH altitude is related to the Home Point. Make sure the RTH altitude is higher than any obstacle in the area.

claims.text: The manual states: 'The aircraft cannot avoid obstacles during failsafe RTH when there is insufficient light.'
claims.quote: The aircraft cannot avoid obstacles during failsafe RTH when there is insufficient light.

claims.text: The manual states: 'Exit RTH and use the remote controller to control the aircraft when the remote controller signal is normal.'
claims.quote: Exit RTH and use the remote controller to control the aircraft when the remote controller signal is normal.

claims.text: The manual states: 'During RTH, continue to check the liveview and the aircraft altitude in case failsafe is disabled due to the GNSS signal icon having less than three bars.'
claims.quote: During RTH, continue to check the liveview and the aircraft altitude in case failsafe is disabled due to the GNSS signal icon having less than three bars.
conditions: GNSS signal has fewer than three bars
